question_text: According to the course material, GST201 treats Nigerian perception of his world, culture areas of Nigeria and their characteristics, evolution of Nigeria as a political unit, and the concepts of:
option_a: functional education, social justice, individual and national development, norms and values and moral obligations of citizens
explanation: The introduction lists those concepts among the 14 units.

question_text: According to the course material, understanding Nigerian peoples and culture will equip you not only to have a sound knowledge of Nigeria, but also to:
option_c: replace Ile-Ife with Lagos as Oduduwa's landing
explanation: Your understanding will equip you to teach other people too.

question_text: According to the course material, course aims include introducing you to traditional Southern and Northern Nigerian peoples and culture, and helping you understand:
option_a: the evolution of Nigeria as a political unit
explanation: Aims include helping you understand the evolution of Nigeria as a political unit.

question_text: According to the course material, course aims also include highlighting some major culture areas of Nigeria and analyzing:
option_a: the impact of Western education on national development in Nigeria
explanation: Aims include analyzing the impact of Western education on national development.

question_text: According to the course material, on successful completion you should be able to discuss the culture areas of Nigeria and their characteristics, and explain:
option_a: the evolution of Nigeria as a political unit
explanation: Objectives include explaining the evolution of Nigeria as a political unit.

question_text: According to the course material, the leader of the founder lineage in Yoruba towns assumes headship; the head of the town is the Baale, also called Oba when:
explanation: He is also called Oba when crowned king.

question_text: According to the course material, at the local Yoruba level the town is divided into wards; the ward chief is called:
explanation: The ward chief is called Ijoye, Adugbo or Olorin itun.

question_text: According to the course material, Yoruba wards are made up of compounds headed by the eldest man called:
explanation: Compounds are headed by the eldest man called Baale.

question_text: According to the course material, three judicial levels in traditional Yoruba politics are represented by the courts of:
option_a: the Oba, the Ijoye and the Baale
explanation: Three judicial levels: court of the Oba, the Ijoye and the Baale.

question_text: According to the course material, the Alaafin used the Bere annual festival periods to acknowledge:
option_a: the renewal of allegiance of the provincial governors to him
explanation: The Alaafin used Bere annual festival periods to acknowledge renewal of allegiance of provincial governors.

question_text: According to the course material, provincial governments in Oyo were administered by princes, minor kings and baales, all subject to the over-lordship of the Alaafin, who had personal agents called:
explanation: The Alaafin had personal agents, Ilari, all over the provinces.

question_text: According to the course material, theoretically the Alaafin was the fountain of authority and was therefore regarded as:
explanation: The Alaafin was regarded as companion of the gods.
